items.author: CasaHODL
items.context: Casa recuerda que este año hubo un bug de firmware en Coldcard, dispositivos manipulados vendidos por revendedores y fallas en herramientas de autocustodia; recomienda multisig multi-fabricante y anuncia un taller en vivo el 1-dic. Pregunta qué dudas hay sobre multisig.
items.suggested_text: Multi-vendor multisig is a solid answer to vendor risk. The other route is cutting the vendor dependency at the root: an air-gapped signer you build and verify yourself, so no firmware update or reseller sits between you and your keys. More complexity either way, so the real question is which risk you'd rather manage. I wrote up the DIY route here: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HQ5NS31N?dplnkId=c09ef739-11f3-4c76-8c62-92ce160a3341&nodl=1

items.author: just1nvest
items.context: just1n afirma que tener Bitcoin en autocustodia y tener un ETF de Bitcoin no es lo mismo, y que si entiendes Bitcoin, tener control de lo que posees es lo que más sentido tiene.
items.suggested_text: Same price exposure, completely different asset. An ETF share is a claim someone else honors; keys you control are the thing itself. The trade-off is that the security work becomes yours, which is why the setup matters as much as the decision. Here's how I approach it without depending on anyone: https://x.com/forecastquant/status/2119476332635586800

items.author: SimplyBitcoin
items.context: Simply Bitcoin comparte un video con citas de Tony Yazbeck: la autocustodia empieza por entender por qué necesitas control total de tu dinero; por primera vez cada individuo puede ser su propio banco; y nadie debería dictar cómo, dónde y con quién gastas.
items.suggested_text: Understanding the why is step one. Step two is the uncomfortable part: being your own bank also means being your own security team. Most losses I hear about come from the setup, not from Bitcoin. That's the gap I tried to close with a fully air-gapped approach: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0HQ5NS31N?dplnkId=c09ef739-11f3-4c76-8c62-92ce160a3341&nodl=1

items.author: ChartsBtc
items.context: ChartsBTC (bot de gráficos) publica: precio $64,272 vs. precio del power law $146,080; 56% bajo la tendencia, 886 días de atraso; la fecha power law del precio actual sería 2024-06-14. Cifras del autor, modelo propio, no verificadas.
items.suggested_text: 56% below trend is one of the deepest readings the model has shown in years, which is exactly when people stop trusting it. Worth remembering the power law is a long-term trend fit, not a timing tool or a guarantee. I broke down how it works and where it can fail here: https://x.com/forecastquant/status/2118779927340470279 $BTC

items.suggested_text: The sweep below 64K and quick reclaim is the constructive part. The question for me is what happens if 65K AVWAP rejects again: does the deviation low hold, or does it turn into a lower high? Which level would invalidate the compression idea for you? $BTC
